title: Controlling a Stage in Context

header.html: 4.4.1 apply controlling a stage: activities, inputs and outputs, roles and responsibilities, how the practices are applied; 4.4.2 analyze whether the activities, roles and responsibilities are effective and fit for purpose, considering tailoring, the practices, and the purpose and objectives of the process
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves

html:
1Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves

Controlling a stage is the process the project manager uses every day inside a delivery stage. The figure shows the cycle.

Purpose: assign work, monitor it, deal with issues, report progress to the board and take corrective action so that the stage stays within tolerance.

Objectives: work is authorized and agreed first; progress is monitored; issues and risks are handled or escalated; the board is kept informed.

Principle How it shows up here
Manage by exception The project manager acts inside tolerance and escalates only forecast breaches
Focus on products Work packages ask for products with quality criteria
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships The project manager controls, team managers deliver, the board directs
Continued business justification Every issue and risk is checked for its effect on the business case
Exam tip

. If a problem can be corrected inside the stage tolerance, the project manager corrects it and reports it in the next highlight report. Asking the board to decide something inside tolerance breaks manage by exception.

2Activities, inputs and outputs

The names below give the general idea; check the Official Book's wording for the activities.

Activity What the project manager does
Authorize work packages Agrees work with team managers: products, tolerances, quality, reporting
Review work package status Reads checkpoint reports and compares progress with the work package
Receive completed work packages Confirms products are delivered, checked and approved
Review the stage status Compares actuals with the stage plan and forecasts time, cost, scope and benefits
Report highlights Sends the board a highlight report at the agreed interval
Capture and examine issues and risks Records them and assesses the effect on the stage and the business case
Take corrective action Acts inside tolerance to bring work back to plan
Escalate issues and risks Raises anything beyond tolerance or authority to the board
Flow Main items
Inputs from the board Authorization of the stage, the approved stage plan, decisions and advice
Inputs from team managers Checkpoint reports, completed work packages, quality records
Outputs to team managers Authorized work packages
Outputs to the board Highlight reports; exception reports; requests for advice or decisions
Outputs to the records Updated stage plan, registers, daily log, lessons log
Exam tip

. Work starts only through an authorized work package. If an option has a team starting from a chat, a meeting or the stage plan alone, it is not an effective approach.

3Roles

Role Area of focus in this process
Project manager Responsible: authorizes work, monitors, reports, corrects, escalates
Team manager Delivers work packages, sends checkpoint reports, raises issues and risks
Project board Informed by highlight reports; advises; decides when an exception is escalated
Executive Owns the business case; acts when the stage's justification is at risk
Senior user and senior supplier Provide user and supplier resources; help solve problems in their area
Project assurance Checks progress, risks and quality independently for the board
Change authority Decides changes inside its delegated authority
Project support Keeps the logs and registers; helps collect progress data

Check the book's roles table for this process. The general rule: the project manager is responsible, the board is informed and decides only on escalation, and team managers report to the project manager, not to the board.

4How the practices are applied

Practice How it is applied in controlling a stage
Business case Check each issue, risk and change for its effect on benefits and cost
Organization Work flows through the agreed team structure and roles
Plans The stage plan is the baseline; each work package carries tolerances
Quality Work packages include product descriptions; quality records are reviewed
Risk Review the risk register each cycle; act early; escalate what is beyond tolerance
Issues Capture and examine, then send to the right authority: project manager, change authority or board
Progress Reports, forecasts, tolerances and escalation by exception

5Judging a scenario

Effective approach Red flag: not fit for purpose
Work authorized through work packages that state products, tolerances, quality and reporting Work starts from a verbal request, or the team sets its own scope
Tolerances watched and forecasts updated at every review Reviews look only at past actuals, so a breach is seen too late
Exception report as soon as a breach is forecast A breach is hidden, fixed quietly or left for the next highlight report
Corrective action inside tolerance taken by the project manager The board is asked to decide routine matters inside tolerance
Issues and risks examined for their effect on the business case A change is accepted without checking cost and benefit
The project manager keeps control while team managers deliver Control is delegated to a team manager or supplier
Lessons captured as they arise Lessons left until the end of the project

Tailoring changes the form, never the control:

  • Agile teams: a work package can be an iteration. The team plans its own tasks, but the project manager still agrees outcomes, tolerances and reporting.
  • Small projects: fewer documents and short verbal updates, if the board agrees first. Keep the record in the daily log.
  • Large or multi-supplier projects: many team managers, a common report format, project support to consolidate.
  • Sustainability, digital and data: track sustainability targets and use tool data, following the digital and data management approach.
Exam tip

. Tailoring lightens the form, never the control. An answer that drops authorization, tolerances or escalation fails. A shorter report the board agreed to can pass.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1In the build stage of Project Harbor, Wei Chen forecasts that one work package will finish three days late. The stage is still forecast to finish well inside its two-week time tolerance. Sam Okafor sends the board an exception report. Was this an appropriate action for the project manager to take, and why?

  • AYes, because the board must be told about every delay, however small
  • BYes, because any late work package breaks the approved stage plan
  • CNo, because the project manager can correct this inside the stage tolerance
  • DNo, because the team manager is the person who raises exception reports
Show the answer

Answer: C. The stage stays in tolerance, so the project manager takes corrective action and reports it in the highlight report (manage by exception).

S2Sam Okafor sends Wei Chen's team a short message: build the permit form soon and keep the cost reasonable. It names no tolerances, quality criteria or reporting. Was this an appropriate action for the project manager to take, and why?

  • AYes, because a trusted team manager can set the tolerances and quality alone
  • BYes, because the stage plan already holds every work package tolerance
  • CNo, because the project board must approve every work package personally
  • DNo, because the work package should state products, tolerances and quality
Show the answer

Answer: D. A work package is how work is authorized, so it must give the products, tolerances, quality and reporting for the team manager to agree.

S3Project Harbor's build stage has a cost tolerance of plus or minus 10 percent. Sam Okafor's latest forecast shows the stage finishing 12 percent over budget. What should Sam do?

  • ARaise an exception report to the board with options and a recommendation
  • BAgree extra budget with the senior supplier and tell the board later
  • CCut the testing of the remaining products to bring the cost back
  • DDescribe the forecast in the next scheduled highlight report only
Show the answer

Answer: A. A forecast breach of stage tolerance is an exception, so the project manager escalates promptly and the board decides.

S4In the build stage of Project Harbor, a checkpoint report shows one product slipping by two days. The stage stays inside its tolerance. Who decides on the corrective action for the stage?

  • AMarta Quinn, the executive
  • BSam Okafor, the project manager
  • CWei Chen, the team manager
  • DAisha Bello, the assurance lead
Show the answer

Answer: B. Day-to-day control inside tolerance belongs to the project manager, and the board is not asked to decide.

S5Marta Quinn asks for a short, regular summary of build stage progress, issues and risks instead of attending frequent meetings. Which management product should Sam use?

  • ACheckpoint report
  • BEnd stage report
  • CException report
  • DHighlight report
Show the answer

Answer: D. The highlight report goes from the project manager to the board at regular intervals.

S6A small internal project at Brightwater Port Authority has no team manager. The board agrees that the project manager gives a 20-minute weekly verbal update and records actions in the daily log instead of written highlight reports. Was this appropriate tailoring, and why?

  • AYes, because the board agreed a lighter form and stays informed
  • BYes, because a small project does not need to report progress
  • CNo, because every highlight report must be a written document
  • DNo, because a project without a team manager cannot be controlled
Show the answer

Answer: A. Tailoring may lighten the form of reports when the board agrees and still gets the information it needs.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the purpose of controlling a stage?

Show the answer

To assign work, monitor it, handle issues, report progress and take corrective action so the stage stays within tolerance.

R2Who is responsible for the controlling a stage process?

Show the answer

The project manager.

R3Which report does the project manager send to the board at regular intervals?

Show the answer

The highlight report.

R4What must the project manager do when a stage is forecast to exceed its tolerance?

Show the answer

Escalate to the project board with an exception report.

R5Who sets the tolerances for a work package?

Show the answer

The project manager sets them, and the team manager agrees them when accepting the work package.

R6Which principle is the main one behind this process?

Show the answer

Manage by exception.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose assign work, monitor, report, correct, keep the stage within tolerance
Activities authorize, review, receive, report highlights, capture issues and risks, correct, escalate
Inputs stage plan, checkpoint reports, completed work packages, board decisions
Outputs authorized work packages, highlight reports, exception reports, updated logs
Effective work packages, tolerances watched, early escalation, control kept
Red flags verbal work, hidden breaches, board decides routine matters, delegated control
Tailoring lighter form, never lighter control
